props.gloss_en: the baraita: if several kinds of food were before him, he selects and eats, selects and sets aside; and he may not select, and if he selected he is liable to a chatat
Ulla: he selects and eats, and selects and sets aside, for that day; for the morrow he may not select, and if he selected he is liable to a chatat
Rav Chisda: he selects and eats, and selects and sets aside, less than the measure; the measure he may not select, and if he selected he is liable to a chatat

Rav Yosef: he selects and eats, and selects and sets aside, by hand; with a basket or a plate he may not select, and if he selected he is exempt but it is forbidden; with a sieve or a sifter he may not select, and if he selected he is liable to a chatat
Rav Hamnuna: he selects and eats, and selects and sets aside, food from among the waste; waste from among food he may not select, and if he selected he is liable to a chatat
Abaye: he selects and eats, and selects and sets aside, for immediate use; for [later] that day he may not select, and if he selected he is as one selecting for storage and liable to a chatat
Abaye: one who selects for [later] that day is as one selecting for storage
Rav Ashi's tradition: two kinds of food before him, and he selected and ate, selected and set aside -- exempt
R' Yirmeya of Difti's tradition: [in that case] liable
this [exempt] is with a basket or a plate
that [liable] is with a sieve or a sifter
Rav Dimi: it was Rav Beivai's Shabbat, and R' Ami and R' Asi happened by; he threw a basket of fruit before them
Rav Dimi, first possibility: [he did so] because he holds food from among waste is forbidden
Rav Dimi, second possibility: [he did so] because he intended generosity
Chizkiya: one who selects lupines from among their waste is liable
(entertained) Chizkiya holds that [selecting] food from among waste is forbidden
lupines are different -- it is like [selecting] waste from among food
for it is boiled seven times, and if one does not take it [out] it rots

questions.gloss_en: Rav Dimi: I do not know whether Rav Beivai did so because he holds food from among waste forbidden, or because he intended generosity
